decisions.reason: The candidate already requires white text without text effects under project-persistent scope; expanding the separate clean-editing requirement does not change this state.
B-roll integration is an independent rule introduced directly by message 187 and is already fully represented; the clean-editing scope change adds no further effect.
The background-music mix is a separate audio rule for the assigned batch, and project-persistent scope for clean visual editing does not necessarily extend that rule.
The substantive-moment standard is already project-persistent and remains unchanged by the clean visual-editing scope update.
Message 187 already has a target-specific MODIFY for standalone understandability; the separate clean-editing scope change requires no additional candidate update.
The permitted source collection already covers Arden Vale's long-form YouTube videos, and the visual-editing scope change does not alter source-selection rules.
Message 187 does not change the existing good-hook criterion, and persistence of clean visual editing does not propagate to hook selection.
The candidate already requires a project-persistent 70-to-85-second duration, so message 187 merely restates the existing range without changing its state.
Message 187 specifies caption color and effects but does not identify or change the required brand font; the clean-editing scope update cannot safely supply missing font scope.
The twelve-clip production batch and its resumption are already represented by same-message Events; the clean-editing scope change adds no batch-delivery update.
Approval-gated publishing is independently and completely introduced by message 187; expanding clean visual editing does not modify its approval rule.
The twelve-clip launch batch does not necessarily resume or modify the deferred monthly 140-approved-clip obligation, and the clean-editing scope change has no direct effect on that quota.
